blockers.summary: Regression mentioned: "…two commits in one to not introduce a regression by doing them separately. There were small changes required to unit tes…" (hudson-openstack)

The fix only takes effect when the non-default option ovn.ovn_emit_need_to_frag is set, and it needs an OVN version that supports gateway_mtu. The SRU must document this and the minimum OVN version in Ubuntu, otherwise the reported drops persist for default deployments.

The backport to stable/2024.2 and stable/2024.1 squashes the fix together with the follow-up regression fix (bug 2105383), with conflict resolutions and modified unit tests. The SRU must include both changes and test the regression scenario, namely the redirect-type calculation when the gateway port is attached.

The proposed fix covers only the create, attach and update code paths. Comment 25 also called for a maintenance task to update existing routers and networks, and none was merged. Existing deployments may therefore stay affected after the upgrade unless routers are touched, and this is not documented as a limitation.

Ceph 19.2.6 removes the `auth_supported` option, so libvirt RBD storage pools on noble fail to start ('failed to set RADOS option: auth_supported'). This was reproduced with only archive packages and is a regression for noble hosts. It remains unresolved: the ceph package has not been re-spun with the option restored, and libvirt fix LP #2172324 is still pending.

The SRU team (raof) wants the ceph upload re-spun, or replaced by 19.2.7, with the `auth_supported` removal reverted. No such upload exists yet, so the current noble-proposed 19.2.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 should not be released.

The block-proposed-noble tag is still set. The SRU team has been asked to keep the package in proposed until libvirt LP #2172324 is sorted out, and the prerequisite 20.2.4 uploads to resolute and stonking have not been confirmed released.

The release order and version-skew between ceph and libvirt are not handled. Users who upgrade only one of them would regress, so a Breaks/conflict relationship against older libvirt versions is suggested if the libvirt fix is the route taken.

Upgrade-path regression window: 19.2.6 contains the CephX CVE fix, and users moving to a 20.x build without it would hit authentication failures. 20.2.4 must be released to resolute and stonking before or alongside 19.2.6, and this is still in progress.
The autopkgtest regression for libvirt on arm64 was reported and never shown to be resolved. It is probably related to the auth_supported breakage.

Verification was done before the auth_supported regression was found. The OpenStack/charm test run did not catch it, and a re-spun package will need re-verification. The verification-caracal-needed tag is also still outstanding.

comments.author: whershberger
comments.body:
There are two standing issues with these patches:

- get_global_pool_hard_max_size parses /proc/sys/vm/max_map_count incorrectly, resulting in the default value being used unconditionally
- The default value returned by get_global_pool_hard_max_size is UINT_MAX; a better/conservative choice would be the kernel's default max_map_count (65530)

We've submitted upstream patches to resolve both of these issues; neither have been merged to qemu's master yet.

https://lists.gnu.org/archive/html/qemu-devel/2026-10/msg04337.html

findings.message: Newer version(s) of 'ceph' already published for noble: 19.2.6-0ubuntu0.24.04.1 in noble/Proposed/Published. Current version '19.2.3-0ubuntu0.24.04.4' may be outdated.

blockers.summary: The reviewer asked about the jammy patch's DEP3 header: Author is given as pponnuvel, but the referenced upstream commit has a different author. The uploader has not answered, and the header needs correcting.

The Noble debdiff is based on 19.2.3, but 19.2.6 is already in -proposed. The debdiff needs to be rebased onto 19.2.6, otherwise it would conflict with or regress that version. It was promised but has not been posted.

The SRU description says the fix covers Quincy and Squid only, and the Jammy and Noble debdiffs are attached. Yet the Noble fix is only a backport from an unreleased 19.2.7 PR, and the Jammy fix is a custom adaptation of upstream work (PR 58173 is an architecture refactor). Neither patch has been validated upstream as a backport. The description also needs reconciling with this.

The test plan relies on a stress script that crashes only within minutes. There is no recorded evidence that the reproducer crashes on the unpatched package or that the PPA build survives it. The plan also gives no jammy/noble-specific steps and no scrub regression check, even though the description lists 'scrubs not scheduled' as a regression risk.

The Impact section is a placeholder, and the Where-problems-could-occur section claims a deadlock review of the call sites without detail. The Jammy and Noble builds may differ in locking paths, so this needs verification for each series.
